# HyperXosist-Agent

> Convert noisy X/Twitter discussions into actionable engineering signals.
> Discover customer pain points and product feedback, reduce low-signal noise, and generate implementation-ready handoffs for AI coding agents.
> Designed for product research, noise-reduced social listening, market intelligence, and Feedback-to-Fix workflows.
> Generates search plans, official X search URLs, filtering results, and structured handoffs; it does not directly scrape X.

## What it solves

Product teams and coding agents need a reproducible path from public feedback discovery to implementation work. Raw X searches can contain complaints, feature requests, generic praise, engagement bait, giveaways, and other noise. HyperXosist-Agent structures the discovery process, extracts actionable signals from supplied feedback, and packages keep-only evidence for downstream engineering workflows.

## Best for

- Customer pain-point discovery and product-feedback discovery
- Noise-reduced social listening and market research
- UX friction, bug-report, feature-request, and product-improvement research
- AI coding agent workflows that need implementation-ready handoffs
- Human researchers using the browser and shell-based or tool-calling agents
- GPT, Claude, Grok, Llama, OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible, and local runtimes

## Input -> processing -> output

Input may be a natural-language research intent, structured search fields, or feedback text supplied by a user or agent.

Processing follows:

Problem discovery -> search planning -> noise reduction -> signal extraction -> engineering handoff -> Feedback-to-Fix implementation.

Output is structured JSON and, where supported, Markdown containing search plans, scores, official X search URLs, filtering decisions, keep-only signals, Signal-to-Fix inputs, and coding-agent prompts. The system does not claim to scrape X or automatically deploy code.

## Outputs

- Multi-angle search plans for complaints, bugs, feature requests, and product feedback
- Official `x.com/search` URLs and validated query strings
- Noise-reduction rules with Low / Medium / High presets and editable custom terms
- Signal filtering results with keep, reduce, or discard decisions and reasons
- Keep-only JSON exports for downstream agents
- Structured Signal-to-Fix and handoff packages
- Model-agnostic implementation prompts and optional Grok Build prompts
- JSON and Markdown representations for tool-calling and human review

## Remote MCP

- Endpoint: `https://mcp.kgninja.dev/mcp`
- Health: `https://mcp.kgninja.dev/health`
- Transport: Streamable HTTP
- Free tools: `hyperxosist_search_plan`, `hyperxosist_filter_signals`, `hyperxosist_build_handoff`
- Free MCP operations: `initialize`, `tools/list`, planning, filtering, and handoff

Connect an MCP client to the endpoint, call `initialize`, call `tools/list`, then select the tool matching the current stage: search plan, signal filtering, or engineering handoff.

## Free vs paid boundary

Free:

- Human browser UI and manual use of generated official X URLs
- MCP discovery, planning, filtering, and handoff
- Local planning, scoring, noise-rule inspection, and dry-run workflows

Paid:

- Automated production use of generated search URLs
- Automated external collection
- Paid execution at `POST https://api.kgninja.dev/hyperxosist-query`

The paid endpoint returns HTTP 402 until valid x402 payment proof is supplied and returns HTTP 200 after successful execution. Current requirements are published at `https://api.kgninja.dev/payment-options.json`.

The documented price is 0.01 USDC on Base (`eip155:8453`) when confirmed by the current payment metadata. Do not assume payment details from this file if `payment-options.json` differs.

## Quickstart

Remote MCP:

```text
Connect to https://mcp.kgninja.dev/mcp
Call initialize
Call tools/list
Call hyperxosist_search_plan with a natural-language intent
```

Local CLI:

```bash
npx hyperxosist plan "Find product feedback about Acme for PR specs" --json
npx hyperxosist keep --product Acme --feedback '["Users cannot complete onboarding"]' --export-keep-only --json
npx hyperxosist handoff --product Acme --feedback '["Users cannot complete onboarding"]' --json
```

Local library:

```js
const HyperXosistAgent = require('./agent-api.js');
const plan = HyperXosistAgent.planFromIntent('Find product feedback about Acme for PR specs');
const filtered = HyperXosistAgent.filterKeepSignals(['Users cannot complete onboarding']);
const handoff = HyperXosistAgent.buildHandoffPackage({ productName: 'Acme', feedback: filtered.texts });
```

## Tool calling and CLI

Use `toOpenAITools()` or `toAnthropicTools()` to register local tool schemas, then route calls through `dispatchToolCall(name, args)` or `runTool`. Available local dispatch names include:

- `hyperxosist_plan_from_intent`
- `hyperxosist_build_query`
- `hyperxosist_score_query`
- `hyperxosist_filter_keep_signals`
- `hyperxosist_export_keep_only`
- `hyperxosist_build_handoff`
- `hyperxosist_signal_to_fix_pipeline`
- `hyperxosist_build_agent_prompt`

## Detailed workflows

The linked Signal-to-Fix workflow converts keep-only feedback into a structured downstream implementation handoff:

```text
plan -> score -> authorized x402 execution when needed -> official X search -> supplied feedback -> keep-only filter -> handoff -> Signal-to-Fix or coding agent
```

Use `buildSignalToFixPipeline`, `buildHandoffPackage`, `exportKeepOnlyJson`, and `buildAgentPrompt`. Optional Grok Build helpers are disabled by default and are for one-small-change prompts.

## Safety and payment rules

- Do not initiate payment without applicable user or operator authorization.
- If a wallet requires human approval, ask the operator to review and approve it, then retry the same request with valid x402 proof.
- Never request, expose, or log private keys, seed phrases, wallet secrets, or raw payment credentials.
- Do not send sensitive user data or treat synthetic demo feedback as real user feedback.
- GitHub Pages is not the payment verifier; payment verification and settlement remain on the external x402 Worker.
- Planning tools are not a payment bypass for automated production use.
